سورة آل عمران
الدرس العاشر
أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم اللهم صل على سيدنا محمد الفاتح لما أغلق والخاتم لما سبق ناصر الحق بالحق والهادي إلى صراطك لمستقيم وعلى آله حق قدره ومقداره العظيم ورضي اللّٰه تعالى عن أصحاب رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظير ياهمة الشيخ احضري لنا بهذا المحضر
ولتعطفي بنظرة
تأتي لنا بالظفر

(يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةِ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَبَضْلٍ) الشهداء يستبشرون بثواب اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى وفضله زيادته عليه (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ألْمُومِنِينَ) بل يأجرهم. الشهداء وصفهم اللّه في القرآن بأنّهم أحياء عند ربّهم. الشهيد لا يسقط إلا وقد اهتدى لمقعده في الجنة، يوضع على رأسه تاج الكرامة، ويغفر له جميع خطاياه ويشفع في سبعين من أهل بيته، ويزوج اثنتين وسبعين من الحور العين 1، فيستبشرون هذا الثواب وما زادهم اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى من فضله الذي لا حد له. وأنواع الشهادة كثيرة: الشهيد في المعركة شهيد ومن ماتت بجمع، أي امرأة ماتت بالولادة شهيدة، وامرأة ماتت بكرا عذراء، وامرأة ماتت بالغيرة، من صبرت على الغيرة حتى

الله الرعب في قلوب الكفار فتخلفوا عن الميعاد، مدحهم اللّٰه بقوله (الذِينَ فَالَ لَهَمْ التَّاسُ)
نعيم بن مسعود هو فرد ولكن يتكلم عن جماعة {إِلَّ ألتَّاسَ) أبا سفيان وأصحابه (قَدْ جَمَعْواْ لَكُمْ) الجموع ليستأصلوكم (بَاخْشَوْهُمْ) ولا تأتوهم ( جَزَادَهُمُ ) ذلك القول (إيمنا تصديقا بالله ويقينا (وَقَالُواْ حَسْبُنَا أللَّه) كافينا أمرهم (وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ)) المفوض إليه الأمر وهو الله، وخرجوا مع النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم فوافوا سوق بدر فألقى اللّٰه الرعب في قلب أبي سفيان وأصحابه فلم يأتوا وكان معهم تجارات وباعوا وربحوا[2] (بَانقَلَبُوا)
رجعوا من بدر ( بِنعْمَةٍ مِ أللَّهِ وَفَصْلٍ) بسلامة ورزق (لَمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوَءٍ) من قتل أو جرح (وَاتَّبَعُواْ رِصْوَالَ اللَّهِ) بطاعته ورسوله في الخروج (وَاللَّهِ ذُو بَضْلٍ عَظِيمٌ) على أهل طاعته (إِنَّمَا ذَلِكُمُ) القائل لكم إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم ( الشَّيْطَىُ يُخَوِّفْ أَوْلِيَآءَهُ )
الكفار (بَلَاَ تَخَاجُوهُمْ وَخَاجُونِ) في ترك أمري {إِل كُنتُم مُومِنِينَ لا تخافوا أولياء الشيطان، خافوني أنا اللّٰه إن كنتم مؤمنين حقا. هذه الكلمة التي قالها الصحابة «حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيل» بها نصر الله تبارك وتعالى كل نبي وكل ولي من أول الدهر إلى آخر
الدهر .
إبراهيم لما ألقي في النار ماذا قال؟ سأله جبريل: ألك حاجة؟ قال: أما إليك فلا. قال:
ألك حاجة إلى الله؟ قال: نعم. قال: سله ينجيك من هذا، قال: علمه بحالي حسبي عن

سوالي، قال: حسبنا اللَّه ونعم الوكيل، "قَلْنَا يَتَارُ كُوبه بَوْدآً وَسَلْماً عَلَى إِبْرَهِيم". وأصحار النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم لما تجمع الكفار وقالوا «إنَّ ألتَّاسَ فَدْ جَمَعُواْ لَكُمْ بَالحشَوْم جَرَادَهُمْ  إِيمَناً وَقَالُواْ حَسْبَتَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ ألْوَكِيْلٌ بَانْقَلَبُواْ بِنِعْمَةِ مِسَ أللَّهِ وَبَصْلٍ لَمْ يَمْسَسْهَمْ سُوَ) .
واحد من الصالحين يقول: عجبت من شخص توعده رجل أو خاف من شيء وهو يعلم حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وهو يسمع كلام اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى "حَسْبُنَا أللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ أَلْوَكِيلٌ بَانْقَلَبَا ينِعْمَةِ صِ أْللَّهِ وَبَضْلٍ لَمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوَءً"، وأحد نزل به غم وهو يعلم "لاَّ إِلَةَ إِلَّ أَنتَ سُبْحَتَكَ إِنِّي كُنتْ صِنَ الظِّلِمِينَ" وهو يسمع اللّه يقول "قَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَهُ مِسَ ألْعَمٌّ، وأحد تُوعد بالقتل وهو يعرف "وَأْقَوِّضْ أَمْرِىَ إِلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّ أْللَّهَ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ" وهو يسمع اللّٰه يقول: " بَوَفِيهُ أَللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِ مَا مَكَرُواْ وَحَاقَ بِئَالِ مِرْعَوْنَ سُوءُ الْعَذَابِ". هذه الكلمة من لازمها عدد حروفها أربعمائة وخمسين كل صباح ومساء لا يضره شيء مما خلق الله. يقول الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم (رجعنا من الجهاد الأصغر إلى الجهاد الأكبر)1 الجهاد الأصغر الجهاد بالسيف والجهاد الأكبر جهاد النفس والهوى والشيطان. شهيد الجهاد الأصغر شهيد وقتيل الجهاد الأكبر صدّيق والصديقون أعلى مقاما من الشهداء.
ولا بد من الرجوع إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى بالكلية ورفض كل ما سواه وعدم الخوف من أي مخلوق كما أكدت الآية: "وَلاَ تَخَابُوهُمْ وَحَابُونِ"، لن يدخل الحضرة إلا من صلى على جميع الكائنات صلاة الجنازة أربع تكبيرات، فينفرد لله تبارك وتعالى لا يرجو غيره ولا يخافه.
قال أبو يزيد البسطامي: اشتغلت بالمجاهدة لإصلاح نفسي اثنتي عشرة سنة، فرأيت زنارا

ألذِينَ يُسَرِعُونَ فِى الْكُمْرُ يقعون فيه سريعا بنصرته وهم أهل مكة أو المنافقون لا تهتم لكفرهم (إِنَّهُمْ لَنْ يَضْرُّواْ أَللَّهَ شَيا)) بفعلهم وإنما يضرون أنفسهم {يَرِيدُ أَللَّهُ أَلاَّ يَجْعَلٌ لَهُمْ حَظَّاه نصيبا (مِ الآَخِرَة) الجنة فلذلك خذلهم {وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ عَظِيمٌ) في النار والَ ألذِينَ إشْتَرَوْاْ ألْكَفْرَ بِالإيمَلِ أخذوه بدله (لَنْ يَضرُّواْ اللَّهَ) بكفرهم (شَيْئَاً وَلَهَمْ عَذَابُ الِيم مؤلم (وَلا يَحْسِبَىَّ الذِيرَ كَبَرْوَا أَنَّمَا نَمْلِ إملاؤنا (لَهُمْ) أي تأخيرنا لهم بتطويل الأعمار خير لهم (خَيْرٌ لَانجسِهِمّة إِنَّمَا نَمْلِ نمهل (لَهُمْ لِيَرْدَادُواْ إِثْمَا) بكثرة المعاصي (وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ)، ذو إهانة، كانوا يعمرون تسعمائة سنة، ثمانمائة سنة حتى يكونوا كالأقواس من طول العمر 1، وذلك في الكفار ليس بخير لأنفسهم ولذلك روي عن ابن مسعود (ما من نفس برة ولا فاجرة إلا والموت خير لها، إن كانت برة فما عند اللّه خير للأبرار، وإن كانت فاجرة فقد قال اللّٰه "إِنَّمَا نُمْلِ لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُواْ إِثْمَاً ) [2] (خير الناس من طال عمره وحسن عمله وشر الناس من طال عمره وساء عمله) [3] من يعمل خيرا إذا طال عمره فذلك خير له ومن يعمل شرا كلما ازداد عمرا ازداد شرا «وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِيرٌ» ذو إهانة في الآخرة (مَا

والفقير غنيا، كما ترى الحسن سيئا والسيئ حسنا. من شدة حماقة عدو اللّٰه رأى أن اللّٰه عبر يها عن الإنسان لأن أكثر الأفعال تزاول بالأيدي (زَأَنَّ أُلَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلْم)) ذي ظلم (لِلْعَبِيد)) اللّه لا يظلم الناس مثقال ذرة، ظلام صيغة مبالغة، «أللَّةَ لَيْسَ بِظَلِّمٍ» هذا في الظاهر لا يدل على أنه لا يظلم وهو لا يظلم البتة فكيف يوصف مولانا بأنه ليس بظلام وهو ليس بظالم أصلا؟ لأن الخلق كثير لو كان يظلم الخلق لكان ظلاما، لأن من كثر منه الظلم يكون ظلاما. والله تبارك وتعالى لم يصدر منه أي ظلم لأي مخلوق الذِينَ فَالْوَاْ لحمد (إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَهِدَ قد عهد (إِلَيْنَا في التوراة (أَلاَّ نُومِنَ لِرَسُولٍ) نصدقه (حَتَّىٰ يَاتِيَنَا بِفُرْبَادِ تَاكُلُهُ النَّارُ) فلا نؤمن لك حتى تأتينا به، وهو ما يتقرب به إلى اللّٰه من نَعَم وغيرها فإن قُبل جاءت نار بيضاء من السماء فأحرقته وإلا بقي مكانه، وعهد إلى بني إسرائيل ذلك إلا في المسيح عليه السلام ومحمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم، لما جاء المسيح نسخ ذلك ولما جاء محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم كذلك [1] (فُلْ) لهم توبيخا (فَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رُسُلٌ صِ فَبْلِ بِالْبَيِّنَٰتِ) بالمعجزات (وَبِالذِى فُلْتُمْ) كزكرياء ويحي فقتلتموهم ( جَلِمَ فَتَلْتُمُوهُمْو إن كُنتُمْ صَدِفِيَ إن كنتم تؤمنون عند الإتيان بالقربان فهؤلاء أتوا بالقربان وقتلتموهم (قَإِن كَذَّبُوكَ بَفَدْ كُذِّبَ رُسْلٌ مِ فَيْلِكَ جَآءُو بِالْبَيّنَٰتِ) بالمعجزات ( وَالتزَّبُرِ) كصحف إبراهيم وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُنِيرِ) الواضح كالتوراة والإنجيل فاصبر كما صبروا وكُلَّ نَمْسِ ذَائِفَةُ الْمَوْتُ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَجَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ جزاء أعمالكم (يَوْمَ الْفِيَمَةُ) كل من عاش لا بد أن يموت، والجزاء ليس في الدنيا إنما هو في الآخرة (جَمَى زُحْزِحَ) أبعد (عَى البّارِ وَأَدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ بَقَدْ[1]

قَازم من أبعده اللّٰه من النار وأدخله الجنة نال غاية مطلوبه (وَمَا الْحَيَوْةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَ مَتَعْ الْغُرُورُ الباطل يتمتع به قليلا ثم يفنى. الدنيا دار الغرور، متاع قليل ويفنى عما قليل، والآخرة خير وأبقى، فالذي يبقى خير من الذي يفنى، والدنيا فانية والاخرة باقية. كان واحد من الصالحين يتعبد ليلا ونهارا لا يفتر عن العبادة يصوم النهار ويقوم الليل كله، فقيل له: ألا تستريح في بعض الأوقات؟ قال: كم عمر الدنيا؟ قيل له: سبعة آلاف سنة، قال:
كم يوم القيامة؟ قيل: خمسون ألف سنة، قال: لو عشت مدة عمر الدنيا لكان الواجب علي أن أجتهد في جميع أيامها لأنّها قليلة بالنسبة إلى يوم القيامة فكيف بما بعدها؟ والإنسان لابد أن يموت سواء كان صالحا أو طالحا، والمرء مجزى بعمله إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر، والجزاء ليس في الدنيا إنما الجزاء في الآخرة. "وَإِنَّمَا تُوَقَّوْلَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْفِيَايَةُ.
لَتُبْلَوْنَّ) تختبرن (ح أَمْوَلِكُمْ) بالفرائض والجوائح (وَأَنمسِكُمْ) بالعبادات والبلاء
(وَلَتَسْمَعْنَّ مِنَ اْلذِينَ أُوتُواْ الْكِتَابَ مِن فَبْلِكُمْ) اليهود والنصارى (وَمِسَ ألذِيرَ أَشْرَ كَوَا)
من العرب (أَذىً كَثِيراً) من السب والطعن والتشبيب بنسائكم (وَإِن تَصْبِرُوا) على ذلك تتَّفوا اللّٰه جَلَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الأُمُورِ من معزوماتها التي يعزم عليها لوجوها () اذكر { إِذَ آخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيتَوَ ألذِينَ أوتُوا الْكِتَٰبَ) العهد عليهم في التوراة الَيََّه )
أي الكتاب لِلنَّاسِ وَلا تَكْتُمُونَهُ ) أي الكتاب ( قَنَبَذُوه طرحوا الميثاق (وَرَاةَ ظهورِهِمْ ) فلم يعملوا به ولم يعلّموه (وَاشتَرَوْأ بِهِ) أخذوا بدله {تَمَنَا قَلِيلًا ) من الدنيا من سفلتهم برئاستهم في العلم فكتموه خوف فوته عليهم، وهو نعت النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم وآية الرجم (قَبِيسَ مَا يَشْتَرُونَ) شراؤهم هذا. لما وصف الدنيا أنّها متاع الغرور وجب

مدحت أخاك فقد ذبحته [1]، وذلك في حق من إذا مدح نسي ما يعلم في نفسه من النقائص وتعلق بمدح المادحين، ومثاله كمن يقال له إن لما يخرج منك من الغائط رائحة طيبة، فنعان بما سمع وترك ما يعرف، من إذا مدح تكبر بالمدح ونسي ما فيه من الصفات الخية والنقائص ذلك هو الذي يذبحه المدح، ومنهم خاصةٌ إذا مُدحوا رجعوا إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعال بالاستغفار والتواضع، كما كان يفعل سيدنا علي بن أبي طالب أو أبو بكر فكان يقول إذا مُدِح: رب اجعلتي فوق ما يظنون واغفر لي ما لا يعلمون [2]، هذا لا يضره المدح. ومنهم كمّل خواص الخواص يسمعون المدح من اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى على كل حال، المدح لولا أنه صادر من اللّٰه لما وقع، فالكمل يفرحون بكل مدح في حقهم لشهودهم ذلك من الحق تبارك وتعالى أولعك أيضا لا يضرهم المدح. (وَلِلهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَوَتِ وَالأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَدِيرم ومنه تعذيب الكافرين وإنجاء المؤمنين إِلَّ فِي خَلْوِ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ) بما فيهما من العجائب (وَاخْتِلَفِ اليْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ) بالمجيئ والذهاب والزيادة والنقصان لايَت) دلالات على قدرته تعالى لاوْلِي الألْبَبِ هذه الآية نزلت بعد آيات سورة
البقرة تلك ثمان آيات، وهذه ثلاث آيات اختصرها لأنّها تقدمت، من تفكر في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار علم قدرة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى ( الذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ أللَّهَ فِيَاماً وَفُعُوداً وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ أولوا الألباب الذين يذكرون اللّٰه في كل أحوالهم قياما وقعودا

دخل جماعة من الصحابة على عائشة رضي اللّٰه عنها يتقدمهم عبد اللّٰه بن عمر فسلموا على عائشة، قالت: من القوم؟ قالوا: جماعة من أصحاب رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم فينا عبداللّٰه بن عمر. قالت: عبد اللّه بن عمر ما لَكَ لا تزورنا كثيرا؟ قال لها: الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم يقول: (زر غبا تزدد حبا)1 ولكن دعينا من هذا كلا جئنا لنسألك عن أعجب شيء رأيته في رسول اللّه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم فأرسلت دموعها وقالت: كل أحواله عجب ولكن أعجب ما رأيت منه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم أنه دخل علي ذات ليلة في نوبتي فلما قرب مني قال لي: يا عائشة أتأذنين لي في عبادة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى؟ قلت له:
والله أنا لا أحب الآن إلا القرب منكَ ولكن أذنت لك، فتوضاً ووقف يبكي يبكي حتى وصلت دموعه إلى منحره فجلس فاضجع على خده يبكي حتى وصلت دموعه إلى الأرض فدخل بلال يؤذنه بالفجر ورأى ما به فقال: أتفعل هذا يا رسول اللّٰه وقد غفر اللّٰه لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر؟ قال: (أفلا أكون عبدا شكورا)؟2 كيف لا أفعل وقد أنزل علي الليلة هذه الآية "وَيَتَمَكَّرُونَ مِي خَلْوِ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالاَرْضِ". تفكر العامة أن يتفكروا في خلق اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى ليستدلوا بِه على الخالق. وتفكر الخواص في ذات اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى، أما

التفكر في ذات اللّٰه فحرام على العامة لأنهم لا يقدرون أن يكيفوا ذات اللّه تبارك وتعالى التي ليس لها أين ولا كيف ولا قدم ولا رأس ولا يدان، إذا تفكر عامي في هذا يجعل مولانا كبطيخة فقط فيقع فيما لا يحمد. أما الخواص فلهم التفكر في ذات اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى فلهذا ورد: تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة سنة، وورد تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة سبع سنين، وورد تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة سبعين سنة[1].. لكل مقام مقال ( رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَفْتَ هَذَا بَطِلًا )) هذا الخلق الذي نراه إنما خلقته ليدل على كمال قدرتك لا عبثا وسُبْحَنَةً) تنزيها لك (بَفِنَا عَذَابَ ألبَّارٌ رَبَّنَ إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ الثَّارَ فَدَ اخْرَبْتَهُ أهنته (وَمَا لِلظَّلِمِينَ) الكافرين
(ص أنصارِ) يمنعونهم من عذاب اللّٰه تعالى ( رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِياً يُنَادِ لِلايمَنِ) أي إليه وهو محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم أو القرآن (أَنَ) بأن (امِنُواْ بِرَبِّكُمْ جًامَنَّا رَبَّنَا مَاغْمِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا() طلبوا المغفرة من اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى (وَكَبِّرْ عَنَّا سَيِّئَاتِنَا) فلا تظهرها بالعقاب عليها (وَتَوَقَّنَا مَعَ الابْرَارِ) تقبض أرواحنا مع الأبرار الأنبياء والصالحين ( رَبَّنَا وَءَاتِنَا مَا وَعَدَتَّنَا عَلَىٰ رُسُلِكَ) على ألسنة رسلك من الرحمة والفضل، وسؤالهم ذلك - وإن كان وعده تعالى لا يخلف - سؤال أن يجعلهم من مستحقيه لأنّهم لم يتيقنوا استحقاقهم له، وتكرير ربنا مبالغة في التضرع ( وَلَا تُخْزِنَا يَوْمَ الْفِيَمَةٌ إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ) وصف الذاكرين اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى بأنّهم يكثرون من الدعاء ويذكرون اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى. وذِكر اللهِ تبارك وتعالى في البداية باللسان ثم بالقلب ثم بالروح، بذكر اللسان يجد الفناء في الأفعال، وبذكر القلب يجد الفناء في الصفات، وبذكر الروح يجد الفناء الكلي يفنى ثم يفنى ثم يفنى فكان فناؤه عين البقاء. والذكر له قشر ولب ولب لبّ، فالعامة لهم القشر والخاصة لهم[1]

اللب، وخاصة الخاصة لهم لب اللب، لب اللب هو الزيت. على كل حال لابد من الإكثار من ذكر اللّه تبارك وتعالى (بَاسْتَجَابَ لَهَمْ رَبُّهُمة دعاءهم { أَنّهِ لَا أضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَيِلٍ مِنكُم صِ ذَكَّرٍ أوْ انبِئ بَعْصُكْم مِنْ بَعْضِ) سبب نزول هذه الآية أن أم سلمة شكت إلى رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم قالت: ما لي لا أسمع ذكر النساء في الهجرة والجهاد في شيء؟ فقال: «لَا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِنكُم صِ ذَكَرٍ أوْ انبىً بَعْضُكُم مِنْ بَعْضِ»  الذكور من الإنان والإناث من الذكور، إذاً كل ما ذكر اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى في حق الرجال فقد ذكره في حق النساء بَالذِيرَ هَاجَرُوا) من مكة إلى المدينة وَأخْرِجُواْ م دِبْرِهِمْ وَأْوذُّواْ مِ سَبِيلِ) دبني (وَفَتَلُوا) الكفار (وَفُتِلُوا) استشهدوا (لَاكَقِّرَىَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ أسترها بالمغفرة
(وَلَادْخِلَنَّهُمْ جَنَّتِ تَجْرِى مِ تَحْتِهَا ألانْهَرْ تَوَابا) جزاء (مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ) تبارك وتعالى ( وَاللَّهُ عِندَهُو حُسْ الثَوَابِ) الجزاء. أهل الجنة الذين هاجروا من مكة إلى المدينة وهم المهاجرون وأوذوا في سبيلي آذاهم الكفار مع الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم، والرسول يقول: (ما أوذي نبي مثلما أوذيت)2 ومعنى ذلك: ما صفا نبي مثلما صفيت، (أشد الناس بلاء الأنبياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل) [3] أهل الصفاء مع اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى لابد لهم من جيران يؤذوتَهم لابد أن

يحدوا الإذاية ممن عرفوا وممن لم يعرفوا، لأن ذلك هو الذي يصفيهم، الإنسان بطبعه يحب حنسه وقرابته فإذاً إن لم يجد ما يزعجه عن هؤلاء بقي يحبهم أو بقي يقسم لهم قسما وافرا من قلبه، والله يحب أن ينفرد بقلب العبد، فإذاً يصدر له الإذاية من كل جانب، من كل قريب من زوجة، من ولد، من أخ، من كل من يظن ومن كل من لا يظن فيرتحل قلبه ويعلم أن العبد ليس له إلا اللّٰه فيفر إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى برفض كل ما سواه، وإذا استكمله حتى استخلصه رجعه إليهم لينفعهم ولا يتأذى بإذايتهم لا يحس بها. من أحب الجنة فعليه بخمسة أشياء: لا بد أن يترك هوى النفس "وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَي النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْوي فَإِنَّ الجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوي"، إذاً من خالف هوى نفسه فهو من أهل الجنة؛ وأن يترك الدنيا ويشتغل بطاعة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى، ورد في الحديث (ثمن الجنة ترك الدنيا) هما ضرتان من مال إلى واحدة منهما غضبت الأخرى، إذاً من أحب الآخرة ترك الدنيا، والنفس تدعي أنّها تقدر أن تباشر الدنيا وتتناول شهواتها ولا يمنعها ذلك من العمل للآخرة، وذلك من غرورها فقط، ثمن الجنة ترك الدنيا؛ والثالث المداومة على العمل للآخرة "تِلْكُمْ الْجَنَّةُ أورِثْشَوها بِمَا كَنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ"؛ الرابع: لابد من حب الصالحين ومصاحبتهم (المرء مع من أحب) [2] فإنّهم عندما وقفوا بين يدي ربهم يشفعون في إخوانِهِم وأحبابهم وأصدقائهم. ولابد
وهو عند البخاري في صحيحه عنوان باب من كتاب المرضى بلفظ باب: أشد الناس بلاء الأنبياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل.
englishText:
«They rejoice at a favour from Allah and a bounty» — the martyrs rejoice at the reward of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and at His bounty, which is His increase upon it — «and that Allah does not let the reward of the believers go to waste» (Q. 3:171) — rather He rewards them. The martyrs: Allah described them in the Qurʾan as being alive with their Lord. The martyr does not fall without having already been guided to his seat in the Garden; the crown of honour is placed upon his head; all his sins are forgiven him; he intercedes for seventy of his household; and he is wedded to seventy-two of the wide-eyed maidens of Paradise (ḥūr al-ʿīn). So they rejoice at this reward and at what Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has added to them of His bounty, which has no limit. The kinds of martyrdom are many: the one slain in battle is a martyr; and she who dies bi-jumʿ — that is, a woman who dies in childbirth — is a martyr; and a woman who dies a virgin maiden; and a woman who dies of jealousy — she who bore jealousy patiently until

Allah [cast] terror into the hearts of the unbelievers, so they failed to keep the appointment. Allah praised them with His words: «Those to whom the people said»

Nuʿaym b. Masʿūd was a single man, but he spoke on behalf of a group. «Indeed the people» — Abū Sufyān and his companions — «have gathered against you» — the hosts, to root you out — «so fear them» — and do not go out to them — «but it increased them» — that saying — «in faith» — in affirming the truth of Allah, and in certainty — «and they said: Allah is sufficient for us» — sufficient for us against their affair — «and the best of guardians» (Q. 3:173) — the one to whom the matter is entrusted, and that is Allah. They went out with the Prophet ﷺ and arrived at the market of Badr, and Allah cast terror into the heart of Abū Sufyān and his companions, so they did not come. They had trade goods with them, and they sold and made a profit. «So they turned back»

they returned from Badr — «with a favour from Allah and a bounty» — with safety and provision — «no harm having touched them» — of killing or wounding — «and they followed the good pleasure of Allah» — by obeying Him and His Messenger in going out — «and Allah is the possessor of great bounty» (Q. 3:174) — towards those who obey Him — «That is only» — the one who says to you that the people have gathered against you — «Satan, frightening his friends»

the unbelievers — «so do not fear them, but fear Me» — in abandoning My command — «if you are believers» (Q. 3:175). Do not fear the friends of al-shayṭān (Satan); fear Me — I am Allah — if you are truly believers. This word (kalima) which the Companions said, «Allah is sufficient for us, and the best of guardians» — by it Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave victory to every prophet and every walī (friend of Allah) from the beginning of time to the end of

Ibrāhīm, when he was cast into the fire — what did he say? Jibrīl asked him: ⟨Have you any need?⟩ He said: ⟨Of you, none.⟩ He said:

⟨Have you any need of Allah?⟩ He said: ⟨Yes.⟩ He said: ⟨Ask Him to deliver you from this.⟩ He said: ⟨His knowing my state suffices me instead of⟩

⟨my asking.⟩ He said: «Allah is sufficient for us, and the best of guardians». «We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Ibrāhīm» (Q. 21:69). And the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, when the unbelievers gathered and said: «Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them — but it increased them in faith, and they said: Allah is sufficient for us, and the best of guardians. So they turned back with a favour from Allah and a bounty, no harm having touched them» (Q. 3:173–174).

One of the righteous says: ⟨I marvel at a person whom a man threatens, or who fears something, while he knows «Allah is sufficient for us, and the best of guardians», and while he hears the speech of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: «Allah is sufficient for us, and the best of guardians. So they turned back with a favour from Allah and a bounty, no harm having touched them» (Q. 3:173–174); and at one upon whom grief descends while he knows «There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was indeed among the wrongdoers» (Q. 21:87), and while he hears Allah saying: «So We answered him and delivered him from the grief» (Q. 21:88); and at one who is threatened with being killed while he knows «And I entrust my affair to Allah; indeed Allah is seeing of the servants» (Q. 40:44), and while he hears Allah saying: «So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and a terrible punishment encompassed the people of Firʿawn» (Q. 40:45).⟩ This word: whoever keeps to it the number of its letters, four hundred and fifty, every morning and evening, nothing of what Allah has created will harm him. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad.⟩ The lesser jihad is jihad with the sword, and the greater jihad is the jihad against the nafs (the soul), against caprice and against al-shayṭān. The martyr of the lesser jihad is a martyr, and the one slain in the greater jihad is a veracious one (ṣiddīq), and the veracious are higher in station than the martyrs.

One must return to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, entirely, and reject everything other than Him, and not fear any created thing, as the verse (āya) affirmed: «so do not fear them, but fear Me» (Q. 3:175). No one will enter the Presence but he who has prayed over all created beings the funeral prayer, its four pronouncements of ‘Allah is greater’ (takbīr), so that he stands alone for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hoping in no other than Him and fearing no other than Him.

Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī said: ⟨I occupied myself with striving to set my soul right for twelve years, and I saw a belt marking a non-Muslim (zunnār)⟩

«those who hasten into unbelief» — they fall into it swiftly, in support of it, and they are the people of Mecca, or the hypocrites; do not be concerned at their unbelief (kufr) — «indeed they will not harm Allah in anything» — by what they do; rather they harm themselves — «Allah wills not to assign them any share» — a portion — «in the hereafter» — the Garden; and that is why He forsook them — «and theirs is a great punishment» (Q. 3:176) — in the Fire. «Indeed those who have bought unbelief at the price of faith» — they took it in exchange for it — «will not harm Allah» — by their unbelief — «in anything, and theirs is a painful punishment» (Q. 3:177) — hurtful — «And let not those who disbelieve suppose that what We grant of respite» — that is, Our granting of respite — «to them» — that is, Our deferring them by lengthening their lives, is good for them — «is good for themselves» — «We only grant respite» — We give them time — «to them, that they may increase in sin» — through the multitude of acts of disobedience — «and theirs is a humiliating punishment» (Q. 3:178) — one that carries humiliation (ihāna). They used to live nine hundred years, eight hundred years, until they became like bows from the length of their lives; and in the case of the unbelievers that is not good for themselves. For that reason it is reported from Ibn Masʿūd: ⟨There is no soul, righteous or wicked, but that death is better for it. If it is righteous, then what is with Allah is better for the righteous; and if it is wicked, then Allah has said: «We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin» ⟩ ⟨The best of people is he whose life is long and whose deeds are good, and the worst of people is he whose life is long and whose deeds are bad.⟩ Whoever does good: when his life is long, that is better for him; and whoever does evil, the more his life increases, the more his evil increases. «And theirs is a humiliating punishment» — one that carries humiliation, in the hereafter — «Not»

and the poor rich, just as you see the good as evil and the evil as good. Out of the sheer foolishness of the enemy of Allah he held that Allah […]. He expressed the human being by them, because most acts are performed with the hands. «and that Allah is not unjust» — possessed of wrongdoing — «toward the servants» (Q. 3:182). Allah does not wrong people by the weight of a mote. ẓallām (one much given to wrongdoing) is an intensive form. «Allah is not unjust» — on the face of it this does not indicate that He does not wrong, and He does not wrong in the least. So how is our Master described as not being ẓallām when He is not a ẓālim at all? Because created beings are many: were He to wrong created beings He would be ẓallām, since one from whom wrongdoing is frequent is ẓallām. And from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, no wrong at all has issued toward any created thing. «Those who said» — to Muḥammad — «Indeed Allah has enjoined» — He has indeed enjoined — «upon us» — in the Torah — «that we should not believe in any messenger» — that we should credit him — «until he brings us an offering that the fire consumes» (Q. 3:183). So we will not believe in you until you bring it to us. It is what is offered in approach to Allah, of livestock and other things; if it was accepted a white fire came from heaven and burned it up, and if not it remained where it was. He enjoined that upon the Children of Isrāʾīl, except in the case of the Messiah, upon him be peace, and Muḥammad ﷺ. When the Messiah came that was abrogated, and when Muḥammad ﷺ came, likewise. «Say» — to them, in rebuke — «Messengers before me did come to you with the clear proofs» — with the miracles — «and with that which you said» — such as Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā, and you killed them — «so why did you kill them, if you are truthful» (Q. 3:183). If you do believe when the offering is brought, then these men brought the offering and you killed them. «And if they deny you, messengers before you were denied, who came with the clear proofs» — with the miracles — «and the scriptures» — such as the scrolls of Ibrāhīm — «and the illuminating Book» (Q. 3:184) — the clear one, such as the Torah and the Gospel. So be patient as they were patient. «Every soul shall taste death, and you shall only be paid your wages in full» — the recompense of your deeds — «on the Day of Resurrection» (Q. 3:185). Everyone who lives must die, and the recompense is not in this world; it is in the hereafter. «So whoever is removed» — put far away — «from the Fire and admitted to the Garden, he has indeed»

«triumphed» — whomever Allah has put far from the Fire and admitted to the Garden has attained the utmost of what he sought — «And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion» (Q. 3:185) — the false, which one enjoys a little and which then passes away. This world is the abode of delusion: a scant enjoyment, and it passes away before long; and the hereafter is better and more lasting. What remains is better than what passes away, and this world passes away while the hereafter remains. One of the righteous used to worship by night and by day, never slackening in worship; he would fast the day and stand the whole night in prayer. He was asked: Will you not rest at some times? He said: How long is the life of this world? He was told: seven thousand years. He said:

How long is the Day of Resurrection? It was said: fifty thousand years. He said: Were I to live out the whole span of this world, it would be my duty to strive through all its days, because they are few beside the Day of Resurrection — so what of what comes after it? A human being must die, whether he is righteous or corrupt, and a man is requited for his deed: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil; and the recompense is not in this world — the recompense is in the hereafter. «and you shall only be paid your wages in full on the Day of Resurrection» (Q. 3:185).

«You shall surely be tried» — you shall be tested — «in your possessions» — through the obligatory dues and through blights — «and in yourselves» — through acts of worship and through affliction

«and you shall surely hear from those who were given the Book before you» — the Jews and the Christians — «and from those who associate others with Allah»

among the Arabs — «much hurt» — abuse, slander, and the composing of love-verses about your women — «And if you are patient» — over that — «and are godfearing» — of Allah — «then that is among the matters of firm resolve» (Q. 3:186) — among the things resolved upon, which are resolved upon because they are obligatory. «And» — recall — «when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book» — the compact laid upon them in the Torah — «that you shall surely make it clear»

that is, the Book — «to the people, and not conceal it» — that is, the Book — «but they cast it» — they threw the covenant — «behind their backs» — so they neither acted upon it nor taught it — «and they bought with it» — they took in its place — «a small price» — of this world, from their underlings, through their leadership in learning; and so they concealed it for fear of forfeiting it. It is the description of the Prophet ﷺ and the verse of stoning. «so evil is what they buy» (Q. 3:187) — this buying of theirs. When He described this world as the enjoyment of delusion, it became necessary

⟨you have praised your brother, you have slaughtered him⟩, and that holds in the case of one who, when he is praised, forgets the shortcomings he knows in himself and attaches himself to the praise of those who praise him. His likeness is one who is told that what comes out of him as excrement has a pleasant smell, and he is content with what he heard and leaves aside what he knows. Whoever, when he is praised, grows proud through the praise and forgets the base (khasīsa) attributes and the shortcomings that are in him — that is the one whom praise slaughters. Among them are an elect who, when they are praised, return to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with asking forgiveness and with humility, as our master ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib used to do, or Abū Bakr; when he was praised he would say: ⟨My Lord, make me above what they suppose, and forgive me what they do not know⟩. Praise does no harm to this one. Among them are the perfected, the elect of the elect: they hear praise from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in every condition. Were the praise not issuing from Allah it would not have occurred, and so the perfected rejoice at every praise given them, because they witness it as from al-Ḥaqq, Blessed and Exalted. Those too are not harmed by praise. «To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is powerful over all things» (Q. 3:189). Part of that is the punishment of the unbelievers and the deliverance of the believers. «Indeed in the creation of the heavens and the earth» — with the wonders that are in them — «and the alternation of night and day» — by coming and going, and by increase and decrease — «there are signs» — indications of His power, Exalted — «for those possessed of understanding» (Q. 3:190). This verse was revealed after the verses of Sūrat

al-Baqara. Those are eight verses, and these are three verses, which he abridged because they had come earlier. Whoever reflects on the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day knows the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides» (Q. 3:191). Those possessed of understanding are those who remember Allah in all their states, standing and sitting

A company of the Companions came in upon ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, with ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar at their head, and they greeted ʿĀʾisha. She said: Who are these people? They said: A company of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; among us is ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar. She said: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar, why is it that you do not visit us often? He said to her: The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨Visit at intervals and you will be loved the more⟩. But spare us all this. We have come to ask you about the most wondrous thing you ever saw in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She let her tears flow and said: All his states were wondrous, but the most wondrous thing I saw of him ﷺ is that he came in upon me one night, on my turn, and when he drew near to me he said to me: ʿĀʾisha, will you give me leave to worship Allah, Blessed and Exalted? I said to him:

By Allah, right now I love nothing but to be near you — but I give you leave. So he performed the ablution and stood weeping, weeping, until his tears reached his breast. Then he sat down, then he lay over on his cheek weeping until his tears reached the ground. Bilāl came in to call him to the dawn prayer and saw the state he was in, and said: Do you do this, Messenger of Allah, when Allah has forgiven you what went before of your sin and what came after? He said: ⟨Shall I not then be a thankful servant?⟩ How should I not do it, when this verse was sent down upon me tonight: «and they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth» (Q. 3:191). The reflection of the common people is that they reflect on the creation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, so as to infer the Creator from it. The reflection of the elect is on the Essence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. As for

reflection on the Essence of Allah, that is forbidden to the common people, because they are not able to conceive a modality for the Essence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, which has no where and no how, no foot and no head and no two hands. When a common man reflects on this he makes our Master into a mere melon, and so he falls into what is not praiseworthy. As for the elect, reflection on the Essence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, belongs to them. For this reason it has come down: ⟨An hour’s reflection is better than a year’s worship⟩, and it has come down: ⟨An hour’s reflection is better than seven years’ worship⟩, and it has come down: ⟨An hour’s reflection is better than seventy years’ worship⟩. Each station has its own saying. «Our Lord, You did not create this in vain» — this creation that we see, You created it only to point to the perfection of Your power, not in sport — «glory be to You» — declaring You free of all imperfection — «so guard us from the punishment of the Fire» (Q. 3:191). «Our Lord, whomever You admit to the Fire, him You have disgraced» — You have humiliated him — «and the wrongdoers have no» — the unbelievers —

«any helpers» (Q. 3:192) — who would ward off from them the punishment of Allah, Exalted — «Our Lord, we have heard a caller calling to faith» — that is, to it; and he is Muḥammad ﷺ, or [it is] the Qurʾan — «that» — meaning: that — «believe in your Lord. And we have believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins» — they sought forgiveness from Allah, Blessed and Exalted — «and absolve us of our evil deeds» — so do not make them manifest by punishing for them — «and take us in death with the righteous» (Q. 3:193) — take our souls with the righteous: the prophets and the pious — «Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers» — upon the tongues of Your messengers, of mercy and of bounty. Their asking for that — even though His promise, Exalted, is not broken — is a request that He make them of those who deserve it, since they were not certain of their deserving it. And the repetition of «Our Lord» is an intensification of entreaty. «and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Surely You do not break the promise» (Q. 3:194). He described those who remember Allah, Blessed and Exalted, as making much supplication and as remembering Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is at the beginning with the tongue, then with the heart, then with the spirit. By the remembrance of the tongue he finds annihilation in the acts; by the remembrance of the heart he finds annihilation in the attributes; by the remembrance of the spirit he finds the total annihilation — he is annihilated, then annihilated, then annihilated, and so his annihilation is the very same thing as subsistence. Remembrance has a husk, and a kernel, and a kernel of the kernel. The common people have the husk, and the elect have

the kernel, and the elect of the elect have the kernel of the kernel. The kernel of the kernel is the oil. In any case, there must be much remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «So their Lord answered them» — their supplication — «I do not let the work of any worker among you go to waste, whether male or female; you are of one another» (Q. 3:195). The occasion of this verse’s revelation is that Umm Salama complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: Why is it that I hear no mention of the women in the hijra and the jihad at all? And he said: «I do not let the work of any worker among you go to waste, whether male or female; you are of one another». The males are from the females and the females from the males. So everything Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has mentioned concerning the men, He has mentioned concerning the women. «So those who emigrated» — from Mecca to Medina — «and were driven out of their homes and were harmed in My way» — My religion — «and fought» — the unbelievers — «and were slain» — they were martyred — «I shall surely absolve them of their evil deeds» — I shall cover them over with forgiveness

«and I shall surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers run, as a reward» — a recompense — «from Allah» — Blessed and Exalted — «and with Allah is the best of rewards» (Q. 3:195) — the best of recompense. The people of the Garden are those who emigrated from Mecca to Medina, and they are the Muhājirūn, and who «were harmed in My way» — the unbelievers harmed them, along with the Messenger ﷺ. And the Messenger says: ⟨No prophet was harmed as I have been harmed⟩, and the meaning of that is: no prophet was purified as I have been purified. ⟨The severest of people in trial are the prophets, then the most like them, then the next most like them⟩. Those who have purity with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, must have neighbours who harm them; they must

find the harm from those they know and from those they do not know, because that is what purifies them. Man by his nature loves his own kind and his kin, and so if he finds nothing to unsettle him away from these, he goes on loving them, or he goes on apportioning them an ample share of his heart; and Allah loves to have the servant’s heart to Himself alone. And so harm issues to him from every side: from every relative — from a wife, from a child, from a brother — from everyone he would expect and from everyone he would not expect. Then his heart departs, and he knows that the servant has none but Allah, and he flees to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, by rejecting everything other than Him. And when He has perfected him, until He has taken him wholly for Himself, He returns him to them so that he may benefit them, and he is not harmed by their harming him; he does not feel it. Whoever loves the Garden must hold to five things. He must leave the caprice of the nafs: «But as for him who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from caprice, the Garden shall be the refuge» (Q. 79:40–41). So whoever opposes the caprice of his nafs is of the people of the Garden. And that he leave this world and occupy himself with obedience to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. It has come in the hadith: ⟨The price of the Garden is leaving this world⟩. They are two co-wives: whoever inclines to one of them, the other is angered. So whoever loves the hereafter leaves this world. The nafs claims that it is able to take up this world and to reach for its appetites and that this will not keep it from working for the hereafter; and that is only from its own delusion. The price of the Garden is leaving this world. And the third is perseverance in working for the hereafter: «This is the Garden; you have been made to inherit it for what you used to do» (Q. 7:43). The fourth: he must love the pious and keep their company — ⟨a man is with whom he loves⟩ — for when they stand before their Lord they intercede for their brothers and their beloveds and their friends. And there must

of supplication (duʿāʾ): asking for the Garden from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨The servant, when he says: ‘My Lord, admit me to the Garden, my Lord, admit me to the Garden, my Lord, admit me to the Garden’ — three times — the Garden says: ‘My Lord, admit him to the Garden,’ and he enters the Garden. And when the servant says: ‘My Lord, grant me refuge from the Fire, my Lord, grant me refuge from the Fire, my Lord, grant me refuge from the Fire,’ the Fire says: ‘My Lord, grant him refuge from the Fire,’ and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, grants him refuge.⟩ So whoever loves the Garden must hold to these five traits: opposing caprice, renouncing this world, loving the righteous, working for the hereafter, and supplication. Much supplication: he asks Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to give him the Garden. «And Allah — with Him is the best of reward» (Q. 3:195). «Let not the going to and fro of those who disbelieve in the land deceive you» (Q. 3:196). When the Muslims said:

The enemies of Allah are in what we see of good, while we are in hardship. The Muslims are the beloved of Allah, and they are always in toil, while the enemies of Allah — the Pharaohs, the reprobates and the dissolute — have of this world what cannot be counted. «Let not the going to and fro of those who disbelieve deceive you» — their moving about — «in the land» — in trade and earning — «a brief enjoyment» — they enjoy it a little in this world and it perishes — «then their abode is Hell, and evil is the resting place» (Q. 3:196–197) — the bedding. No good after which comes the Fire is a good, and no evil after which comes the Garden is an evil. ⟨If this world weighed, with Allah, as much as a gnat’s wing, He would not give an unbeliever a drink of water from it.⟩ Because of the paltriness of this world and its worthlessness with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, Allah has driven it to every Firʿawn and to every

Namrūd and to every reprobate, and He has protected from it every godfearing believer, and every scholar, and every walī. «But those who feared their Lord — for them are gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein» — decreed for everlasting abiding (khulūd) therein — «as a lodging» — it is what is prepared for a guest — «from Allah. And what is with Allah» — of reward — «is better for the righteous» (Q. 3:198) — than the enjoyment of this world. What is with Allah of reward is better for the righteous. «And indeed among the People of the Book there are those who believe in Allah» — such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām — «and in what has been sent down to you» — the Qurʾan — «and what was sent down to them» — the Torah and the Gospel — «humbling themselves» — being lowly — «before Allah»

«They do not sell the signs of Allah» — those which they have in the Torah and the Gospel — «for a small price» — of this world, by concealing them out of fear for their leadership, as others among the Jews do — «Those — theirs is their reward» — the recompense of their deeds — «with their Lord. Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning» (Q. 3:199) — He reckons with creation in the space of half a day of the days of this world. A walī among the awliyāʾ made his way to a bathhouse. He was asked: ‘What do you want?’ He said: ‘I want to enter the bathhouse to wash in it.’ The keeper of the bathhouse said to him: ‘No one enters except for a fee.’ So he turned away weeping. They said: ‘This is an old shaykh who has been barred from the bathhouse, and so he simply weeps.’ He said: ‘No, I did not weep because I was barred from the bathhouse; but if the bathhouse, which is the house of al-shayṭān, is not entered except for a fee, then how shall I enter the presence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, except by works?’ And there was one of the righteous whose garment became soiled and he did not wash it; for the whole of his life he never washed his garment. Someone said to him: ‘Your garment is dirty; there is no harm in your washing it.’ He said: ‘If I wash it, it will get dirty a second time.’ He said: ‘You wash it again.’ He said: ‘Then it gets dirty a third time.’ He said: ‘You wash it again.’ He said: ‘Allah did not create me to busy myself with washing clothes; He created me only to worship Him, Blessed and Exalted.’ And there was one of the righteous, a walī called al-Ḥaddād, who would take fire in his hand and it would not harm him. He was asked about that, and he said that he had become attached to a woman and had solicited her, and she refused, and said:

‘I have a husband.’ So he waited a while, and her husband died, and he asked to marry her, and she refused, and said: ‘I will not […] my children; rather I will guard my children.’ After a time the woman became poor and fell into need, and she came to him asking him for something that she and her children might eat. He said to her: ‘I will not give you anything unless you consent to me in what I asked of you before.’ She said: ‘Yes.’

So he was alone with her. He handed her the money, and she implored Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and said to him that he should let her go for the sake of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He said: ‘I have let you go for the sake of Allah.’ She said to him: ‘May Allah deliver you from the Fire.’ He said: ‘From that day the fire of this world does not burn me, and I hope that the fire of the hereafter likewise will not burn me.’ And there was another youth whom a beautiful woman saw, and she made an attempt on him, and he refused. So she adorned her house with all kinds of ornament and perfumed it, and she sent an old woman to the youth, and she invited him, and he answered the invitation and entered the house and saw the ornaments in it and the kinds of perfume. The woman shut the door and solicited him for himself. The youth said: ‘I am now in need of relieving myself, so let me enter the privy.’ So he entered the privy and relieved himself and smeared himself with the excrement, and when he came out smeared with the excrement the woman said: ‘This one is mad,’ and she merely pushed him, and he went out of her house. Then Jibrīl came to him and said to him: ‘Are you Yūsuf?’ And the excrement turned to perfume, so that the scent of musk wafted from him for the whole of his life, on account of that deed. «O you who believe, be patient» — in acts of obedience and in afflictions, and against acts of disobedience — «and vie in patience» — with the unbelievers, so that they are not more patient than you — «and hold fast» — remain constant in jihad — «and fear Allah» — in all your states — «that you may prosper» (Q. 3:200) — you may win the Garden and be saved from the Fire. A bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: ⟨O Messenger of Allah, I pray five prayers in the day and the night and I add nothing to them, and I fast Ramadan and I add nothing to that; zakat is not incumbent upon me, for I am poor, and the hajj is not incumbent upon me, for I am weak. In which dwelling shall I dwell in the Garden?⟩ The Messenger ﷺ laughed and said to him: ⟨If you guard your two eyes from two things, and your tongue from two things⟩

and your heart from two things, then you are with me in the Garden. If you guard your eyes from looking at what is forbidden and from looking at a person with an eye of belittlement, and guard your tongue from backbiting and from lying, and guard your heart from rancour and from envy, then you are with me in the Garden. «Be patient, and vie in patience, and hold your posts» (Q. 3:200). The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨Shall I not tell you of that by which your evil deeds are effaced for you and your degrees are raised? Performing the ablution thoroughly in spite of what is disagreeable, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the ritual prayer after the ritual prayer — that is the holding of the post, that is the holding of the post, that is the holding of the post.⟩

Sūrat al-Nisāʾ

Medinan. One hundred and seventy-five or one hundred and seventy-six verses (āya).

«By Allah's Name: The Entirely Merciful, The Especially Merciful» «O people» — the people of Mecca — «fear your Lord» — His punishment, by obeying Him — «who»

«created you from a single soul» — Ādam — «and created from it its mate» — Ḥawwāʾ, with the lengthening, from a rib among his left ribs — «and He spread» — divided and dispersed — «from the two of them» — from Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ — «many men and women» — Allah created Ādam with His hand and created Ḥawwāʾ from his left rib, and He spread from the two of them many men and many women likewise, with the adjective omitted, as an indication that women’s right is to be covered. «men» — He brought the attribute — «many»

«and women» — He veiled the attribute — «and fear Allah, by whom you ask one another» — fear Allah by whom you ask one another: when you ask your brother, you say to him, ‘Give me, for Allah’s sake,’ ‘I adjure you by Allah,’ ‘by the right of Allah’ — among yourselves, where one of you says to another, ‘I ask you by Allah’ and ‘I adjure you by Allah’ — «and the ties of kinship» — and fear severing them. They used also to adjure one another by kinship. «Indeed Allah is ever watchful over you» — preserving your deeds and requiting you for them; that is, He has never ceased to be so described (Q. 4:1). In this verse He guided us to godfearing (al-taqwā) and to maintaining the ties of kinship. Kinship (al-raḥim) is derived from al-Raḥmān. al-Ḥaqq says: ⟨Whoever maintains you, I maintain him, and whoever severs you, I sever him!⟩ And the godfearing of Allah, wherever it is mentioned, is compliance with the command and avoidance of the prohibition. As for maintaining the ties of kinship, people differ in that: among them is the rich man, whose maintaining of his kin is by giving of wealth, a gift according to the measure of his means; and whoever is not able to make a gift of any wealth, then service, and visiting, and keeping up contact,

even correspondence by writing — all of this falls within maintaining the ties of kinship. It has come in the hadith that a man may have three days remaining of his life, and when he maintains his kin Allah leaves him thirty years; and a man may have thirty years remaining of his life, and he severs

what is in the tablets of effacement; but as for what is in Umm al-Kitāb, it does not change. «Indeed Allah is ever watchful over you» — preserving your deeds (Q. 4:1). «And give the orphans their property». This verse was revealed concerning an orphan who asked his guardian for his property and he withheld it from him. So the Exalted said: «And give the orphans» — the young who have no fathers — «their property» — when they come of age — «and do not exchange the bad» — the forbidden — «for the wholesome» — the lawful. Do not consume the orphan’s property together with your own property; that is mixing the good with the defective. «And do not consume their property» — joined — «to your property. Indeed it» — the consuming of the property of orphans

«is a crime» — a sin — «great» — grievous (Q. 4:2). «And if you fear that you will not deal justly» (Q. 4:3). This verse was revealed when

they shrank from the guardianship of orphans; and among them was one who had under him ten or eight wives and would not deal equitably among them.

There was a man who had eight orphan girls in his charge whom he would marry, because marrying them cost him nothing, and he would not give them their due, neither in property nor in the apportioning of nights; and this is wrongdoing. So the Exalted said: «And if you fear that you will not deal justly» — that you will not be equitable — «with the orphans» — and so you shrank from their affair — then fear likewise that you will not deal equitably among the women when you marry them: «then marry» — take in marriage — «such as are good for you among the women». So then do not marry the orphan girls for whom you have no

desire; rather, marry such as are good for you among the women. «two by two» — if you wish, marry two at a time — «and three» — three at a time — «and four» — four at a time — and do not go beyond that. It is permissible for a man to marry

one, or two, or three, or four. «But if you fear that you will not be equitable» — this is on condition of equity; so if you fear [that you will act] otherwise than equitably — «then one» — marry her — «or» — confine yourselves to — «what your right hands possess» — of the slave-women

since they do not have the rights that wives have. «That is more apt» — nearer — «that you not deal unjustly» — that you not do wrong (Q. 4:3). «And give the women their bridal gifts» — the plural of ṣaduqa — their dowers — «as a free gift» — a bestowal, a gift, out of a willing heart. They used to marry women and not pay them their dowers; and they would give their daughters in marriage and consume what was brought to them of the dower. «If they willingly remit to you any part of it» — nafsan is an accusative of specification — «then consume it, with relish» — wholesome (ṭayyib) — «and good digestion» — of praiseworthy outcome; there is no harm for you in it in the hereafter (Q. 4:4). «And do not give» — O guardians — «the foolish» — the squanderers among men and women and children — «your property» — that is, their property. The orphan, so long as he has not reached a maturity of judgement fitting him to manage his property, so long as he is foolish, the property is not handed over to him. He attached the orphans’ property to the guardians to confirm the care of it. «which Allah has made for you a means of support» — that by which [livelihood] is maintained — «and provide for them out of it» — feed them from it — «and clothe them, and speak to them a kindly word» — promise them a fair promise that you will give them their property when they reach maturity of judgement (Q. 4:5). «And test» — try them

«the orphans» — before puberty or after puberty, as to their religion and their management of their affairs — «until, when they reach [the age of] marriage» — they become fit for it, by nocturnal emission or by age, which is the completion of fifteen years; this is the school of al-Shāfiʿī, or eighteen years in the school of Mālik, or they attain puberty — «if you perceive» — you discern — «in them maturity of judgement» — soundness in their religion and their property — «then hand over to them their property, and do not consume it» — O guardians — «wastefully» — without right — «and in haste» — hastening to spend it for fear — «that they should grow up» — to maturity of judgement, so that you would be obliged to deliver it to them. «And whoever is» — of the guardians — «rich, let him abstain» — let him keep from the orphan’s property — «and whoever is poor, let him consume in a seemly manner» — to the extent of the wage for his work — «and when you hand over to them» — to

the people — «their property, then call witnesses over them» — that they have taken possession of it — «and Allah suffices as a reckoner» (Q. 4:6) — a keeper of the deeds of His creation and one who brings them to account. It was revealed to rebut the practice of the Jāhiliyya, which gave no inheritance to women or to minors. «For men»

the children and the near kin — «a share» — a portion — «of what the parents and the near kin leave» — the deceased — «and for women a share of what the parents and the near kin leave, of what is little of it» — the property — «or much» — Allah has made it — «an apportioned share» (Q. 4:7)

determined, so that it must be handed over to them. «And when the division is attended by» — the division of the inheritance — «those of kinship» — the relatives from among those who do not inherit — «and the orphans and the poor, then provide for them out of it» — something, before the division — «and say» — O guardians —

«to them» — when the heirs are minors — «a kindly word» (Q. 4:8) — a fair one, by excusing yourselves to them, that you do not own it and that it belongs to minors. Some have said that this is abrogated and some that it is not; but people have made light of leaving it off, and on that view it is a recommendation (nadb), while from Ibn ʿAbbās it is obligatory. «And let fear» — let him be afraid for the orphans — «those who, if they left» — that is, were close to leaving — «behind them» — after their death — «weak offspring» — young children — «would fear for them» — destitution. The guardians fear that they will die and their children will be left young. «So let them fear Allah» — in the matter of the orphans, and let them do for them what they would wish to be done for their own offspring after them — «and let them say» — to one whom death has come upon — «a right word» (Q. 4:9)

correct, by bidding him give in alms less than a third and leave the rest to his heirs, and not leave them destitute. «Indeed those who consume the property of orphans wrongfully» — without right — «consume only in their bellies» — filling them — «fire» — because it ends in fire — «and they will be made to burn» — they will enter — «a blaze» (Q. 4:10) — a fierce fire in which they burn. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, of the night he was taken on the night journey, that he ﷺ passed by a company of men, each of them having a lip like the lip of a camel, and they were being fed morsels of live coals from the Fire which came out from their backsides. He said, ⟨Who are these?⟩ He said, ⟨These are the devourers of the property of orphans.⟩

The opening of this sura speaks of the two hollow parts, the belly and the private parts, and these two are what most brings people into the Fire. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says, ⟨Whoever guarantees to me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee him the Garden.⟩

that is, the tongue and the private parts. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says, ⟨Guarantee me six things and I will guarantee you the Garden:⟩

⟨Be truthful when you speak; when you promise, do not break it; when you are entrusted, do not betray; guard your hands, lower your eyes, guard your private parts, and enter the Garden in peace.⟩ ʿUmar came in upon Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was pulling at his tongue and striking it. ʿUmar said to him, ⟨Gently, Abū Bakr — may Allah forgive you.⟩ He said, ⟨This has brought me to grievous straits and has brought me into the Fire.⟩ Then they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a man asked:

⟨Will Allah hold us to account for what we say?⟩ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ⟨May your mother be bereaved of you! And does anything cast⟩

⟨people down on their faces in the Fire other than the harvests of their tongues?⟩ ⟨Whoever is protected from the evil of his laqlaq (tongue), his dhabdhab (private parts) and his qabqab (belly) has been protected from all evil.⟩ Whoever is protected from the evil of what is between his jaws and his legs has been protected from all evil.

Do you see the opening of this sura? The whole of it speaks of the two hollow parts — the belly and the private parts. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ⟨I entered the Garden and found most of its people to be the poor, and I entered the Fire and found most of its people to be women⟩ — because they curse much and show ingratitude to their husbands. If you were good to one of them for a long while and then she saw in you something that displeased her, she would say, ‘By Allah, I have never seen any good from you.’ Says

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ⟨Two kinds of the people of the Fire I have not seen: men with whips in their hands like the tails of cattle, with which they beat people; and women clothed yet naked, deviating and making others deviate, their heads like the leaning humps of Bactrian camels. They will not enter the Garden, nor will they find its scent, and its scent is found from a distance of five hundred years.⟩ Most of the people of the Fire are women, and what most brings men into the Fire is also women.

«And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them fear Allah, and let them say a right word. Indeed those who consume the property of orphans wrongfully consume only fire in their bellies, and they will be made to burn in a blaze» (Q. 4:9–10).

«He enjoins upon you» — He commands you — «Allah, concerning» — the matter of — «your children» — in what is mentioned — «to the male» — of them — «the like of»

«the share of two females» — when the two of them are joined with him, he has half the property and they have the half. Someone dies and leaves three children, a male and two daughters: the property is divided into two halves, half for the male, and the remaining half is divided between the two daughters. «And if they are» — that is, the children — «women» — only — «more than two» — that is, two and whatever is above them — «they have two-thirds of what he left» — the deceased — «And if she is» — the child born — «one, she has the half, and to his parents» — the two parents of the deceased, the father and the mother — «to each one of them a sixth of what he left, if he has a child» — if the deceased left a child, then the parents have the sixth — «But if he has no child and his parents inherit him» — only, or together with a spouse — «then his mother has the third»

a third of the property — «But if he has brothers and sisters» — that is, two or more, male or female — «then to his mother a sixth». And the remainder

goes to the father, and nothing to the brothers and sisters. «after any bequest he may make, or any debt. Your fathers and your sons — you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit» — in this world and the hereafter. The son does not exclude the father, and the father does not exclude the son, because the wisdom in the inheritance is that whoever has had a walī benefit from his property enters the Garden; and as for the deceased, it is not known which of his heirs are the awliyāʾ, the father or the son. For this reason a share is fixed for the father and a share for the son. «An ordinance from Allah. Indeed Allah is ever knowing» — of His creation — «wise» (Q. 4:11) — in what He has ordained. The questions of the inheritance shares: Allah entrusted them to no prophet and to no angel. He Himself took the division of the inheritance in hand, and that because of people’s miserliness and their greed for property. Had the Messenger been the one who took the division of the inheritance in hand, he would have been accused and treated with enmity, and whoever hates him is wretched with a wretchedness after which there is no felicity ever. And since the apportionment came from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, every one of the heirs was content. «An ordinance from Allah. Indeed Allah is ever knowing» — of His creation — «wise». This is the outward inheritance. As for the real inheritance, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: ⟨We, the company of the prophets, are not inherited from; what we have left behind is alms.⟩ And he said: ⟨The ulama are the heirs of the prophets.⟩ So whoever is born an outward birth has his share of the outward inheritance, and whoever is born a spiritual (maʿnawī) birth has his share of

the spiritual inheritance. To it points the saying of ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace: ⟨He who has not been born twice shall not enter the Presence.⟩ The sensory (ḥissī) birth and the spiritual birth. «And yours is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child, then yours is a fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they may make, or any debt». In this, the child of the son is joined to the child by consensus. «And theirs» — that is, the wives, whether they be several or one — «is a fourth of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child» — by them or by others — «then theirs is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you may make, or any debt. And if a man is inherited from as kalāla» — he has no child and no parent; this is the explanation of kalāla — «or a woman» — inherited from as kalāla — «and he has» — that is, the one inherited from as kalāla — «a brother or a sister» — by the mother; and Ibn Masʿūd read it so — «then to each one of the two a sixth» — of what he left — «But if they are» — that is, the brothers and sisters by the mother — «more than that» — more than one — «then they are sharers in the third» — in which their male and their female are equal — «after any bequest made, or any debt, without causing harm» — without bringing harm upon the heirs — «as an injunction»

Allah enjoins upon you an injunction — «from Allah. And Allah is knowing» — of what He has ordained for His creation in the inheritance shares — «forbearing» (Q. 4:12) — in deferring the punishment of whoever opposes Him. The sunna has restricted the inheritance of those mentioned to such as have in them no impediment, of killing, or difference of religion, or slavery. «Those» — the rulings mentioned, from the matter of the orphans and what comes after it — «are the bounds set by Allah» — His ordinances, which He has set as bounds for His servants that they may act by them and not transgress them — «And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger» — in what He has ruled — «We shall admit him into gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein; and that is the great triumph. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His bounds, We shall admit him» — with both readings — «into a Fire, abiding therein; and he shall have» — therein — «a humiliating punishment» (Q. 4:13–14) — one that carries humiliation. «And those women who»

«commit the indecency» — fornication — «from among your women, call four of you to witness against them». When a man alleges fornication against his wife, he must produce four upright Muslim men who testify that they witnessed the man’s member enter the woman’s private part as the kohl-stick enters the kohl-jar. «If they testify» — against them — «then hold them» — confine them — «in the houses» — and keep them from mixing with people. This was the prescribed penalty for fornication at the beginning of Islam: they used to be confined and did not mix with people — «until death takes them» — the angels of death — «or» — until — «Allah appoints for them a way» (Q. 4:15) — a path to coming out of it. This was at the beginning of Islam. Then, when Allah prescribed flogging, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Allah has appointed a way for them: the unmarried with the unmarried, a hundred lashes and banishment for a year; and upon the married woman, stoning.⟩ And in the hadith, when he had made the penalty plain, he said: ⟨Take from me, take from me — Allah has appointed a way for them.⟩ «And the two who commit it» — that is, the indecency: fornication or sodomy — «from among you» — of the men — «then hurt them both» — with reviling and with beating with sandals — «But if they repent» — of it — «and make amends» — in deed — «then turn away from them both» — and do not hurt them — «Indeed Allah is ever relenting» — toward whoever repents — «merciful» (Q. 4:16) — to him. And this is abrogated by the prescribed penalty. «Repentance with Allah is only» — the repentance whose acceptance Allah has written upon Himself, by His bounty — «for those who do evil» — that is, disobedience — «in ignorance» — that is, being ignorant when they disobey their Lord — «then repent within» — a time — «that is near» — that is, before they come to the death-rattle — «those — Allah relents toward them» — He accepts their repentance — «and Allah is ever knowing» — of His creation — «wise» (Q. 4:17) — in His making. «And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds» — sins — «until, when death comes to one of them» — and he has entered upon the death-throes — «he says» — upon witnessing what he is in — «Indeed I repent now» — that does not profit him, and it is not accepted from him — «nor those who die while they are unbelievers» — likewise, whoever dies before repentance, his repentance is not accepted — «Those — We have made ready» — We have prepared — «for them a painful punishment» (Q. 4:18) — causing pain. «O you who believe, it is not lawful for you». The occasion of this verse’s revelation is what they used to do in the Jāhiliyya. When one of them died, his kinsman came and inherited his wives alone; if he wished, he married them without a bride-gift, and if he wished, he gave them in marriage and took the bride-gift. And when the father died, the son came into his father’s place and married his father’s wife; otherwise he gave her in marriage and took the dower. So the Exalted said: «O you who believe, it is not lawful for you» «to inherit women» — the persons of the women; they are not inherited — «by force» — being compelled to it — «nor» — that you — «hinder them» — prevent your wives from marrying others by keeping hold of them when you have no desire for them, so as to do them harm — «so that you may take away part of what you have given them» — of the dower — «unless they commit a manifest indecency» — fornication or recalcitrance — «and live with them in kindness» — with comeliness in speech, in maintenance and in sharing the night. Whoever marries a woman owes the conditions of marriage: maintenance, clothing, lodging, intercourse and good companionship. Whoever omits one of these five, the wife may divorce herself, and nothing is held against her. «And if you dislike them» — then be patient — «it may be that you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good» (Q. 4:19). When a man marries a woman and stays with her, and after that comes to dislike her, let him be patient in living with her, for in that steadfast patience (ṣabr) he finds much good, which is the reward of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; or Allah provides him a righteous child, and that is much good. There was one of the righteous men who married a bad woman, and she kept on injuring him as long as she lived, until she died. When she died he said, al-Ḥamdu li-Llāh Rabb al-ʿālamīn, and resolved that as long as he lived he would not marry women. When he had stayed some days, he saw in a dream that he was in his mosque and the angels were coming down and passing by him, and whenever an angel passed by him it said: ‘Is this the detested one?’ He said: ‘This is the detested one.’ ‘Is this the one who has lost?’ ‘This is the one who has lost.’ He was alarmed, but he was afraid to ask them, and they went on going back and forth like that. Then he could not restrain himself from asking, and said to them: ‘Who is the loser?’ They said to him:

You. The measure of the deeds of the people of the earth was being raised up for you every day and every night for the whole time of your marriage to the woman and her harming you; and when she died that was cut off, and you came to have no deed. So he awoke, and he married three in one day, and it came about that you would not see him

except that he had three or four with him. This is the meaning of «But if you dislike them, then perhaps you dislike a thing in which Allah has placed much good» (Q. 4:19). The harm a man finds from the mistress of the house — in that there is much reward for him with Allah; or the much good may be that Allah grants him a righteous child. «And if you wish to exchange one wife for another» — taking her in place of the other by divorcing her — «and you have given one of them» — the wives — «a great sum» — much wealth: if you have resolved to part from the woman and you have already given her much in the way of money and household goods — «then take nothing of it» — do not take anything from the woman after the divorce — «would you take it by calumny» — wrongfully — «and manifest sin» (Q. 4:20) — plain. Why do you take this money, when the money was given in exchange for something? «And how could you take it» — on what ground — «when you have gone in» — reached — «one of you to the other», for part of the man has reached part of the woman through the intercourse that makes the dower binding; since she has come to stand in this relation to him, and the cause of that was the money, how can you take this money afterwards? «and they have taken from you a covenant»

a pledge — «solemn» (Q. 4:21) — firm; and that is what the woman sees of the man’s love for her at that time. Or the solemn pledge is the stipulation that is stipulated at the contract. At the contracting of the marriage one says «then retention in kindness or release with good treatment» (Q. 2:229) — this is a stipulation, and the husband must observe this stipulation: he either retains in kindness or releases with good treatment. «And do not marry those women whom your fathers married». The occasion of the revelation of this verse was that a man died, and his son rose and came and sat beside his wife, wanting to take her as a wife after his father. The woman swore that this would never come about from her: after I have been with your father, it is not possible that I should ever be with you. The son said that he would certainly marry her by force, by inheritance. So the two of them brought their case to the Prophet ﷺ, and there was revealed «And do not marry those women whom your fathers married» — a woman whom the father has married, it is not permitted for the son to marry her — «except» — that is, but — «what has already passed» — of your doing: what came before the revelation of the verse is lawful, and after the revelation of the verse this marriage was forbidden — «indeed it»

marrying them — «was an indecency» — something vile — «and detestable» — a cause for the detestation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, which is the most intense hatred — «and evil» — wretched — «as a way» (Q. 4:22) — a road. «Forbidden to you are your mothers» The verse named expressly the women

one of whom it is forbidden for a man to marry. It is forbidden for a man to marry his mothers: his mother, and his mother’s mother, and that one’s mother, and that one’s mother, on up. «And your daughters» — this takes in the daughters of one’s children, however far down: the man’s daughter, and the daughters of his children, and the daughters of those, and the daughters of those, to the end of time. «And your sisters» — from the side of the father or of the mother, likewise: every woman between you and whom there is a sibling bond from the side of the father or of the mother. «And your paternal aunts» — the sisters of your fathers and of your grandfathers. «And your maternal aunts» — the sisters of your mothers and of your grandmothers. «And the daughters of the brother and the daughters of the sister»

— and their offspring are included among them. «And your mothers who have suckled you» — and the mother who suckled the man before the completion of the two years — «and your sisters through suckling» — and joined to that, by the sunna, are their daughters. «And the mothers of your wives, and your stepdaughters» — and your rabāʾib (stepdaughters) is the plural of rabība, and she is the wife’s daughter by a man other than him — «who are in your care»

— whom you rear: a description that accords with what is usually the case, so it carries no counter-implication. What is usual is that the stepdaughter is in his care; but even if she is not in his care, the stepdaughter is forbidden. «of your wives to whom you have gone in» — the stepdaughter who is forbidden is the stepdaughter whose mother the man has gone in to — «but if you have not gone in to them» — if the man has contracted marriage with the woman’s mother and has not gone in to her — «then there is no blame upon you» — it is permitted for him to divorce the mother and marry the daughter, if she accepts — «and the wives of your sons who are of your loins» — when a son of one’s own loins has married a woman, she is forbidden to the father — «and that you should join together two sisters» — whether by lineage or by suckling, in marriage — «except» — that is, but — «what has already passed» — what came before, in the Jāhiliyya, of joining together two sisters: that is lawful — «indeed Allah is forgiving» — of what has passed from you before the prohibition — «merciful» (Q. 4:23). Allah has never forbidden anything in the Qurʾan and excepted what had already passed, save in two cases:

«And do not marry those women whom your fathers married» — He said: «except what has already passed» (Q. 4:22), «and that you should join together two sisters» — He said: «except what has already passed» (Q. 4:23). The reason for this is that these two cases occurred among certain of the forefathers of

the Prophet ﷺ. Kināna married his father’s wife, and among the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ there was one who joined together two sisters. Had it been forbidden and what had already passed not been excepted, this would have touched something of the honour of the Prophet ﷺ; but since the Prophet ﷺ is inviolate in his person, what came before the revelation of the verse is lawful, so that nothing should touch any part of the Prophet ﷺ. This is the wisdom (al-ḥikma) in this exception. These women — marrying them is forbidden. O Allah, bless our master Muḥammad.
arabicBody:
(يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةࣲ مِّنَ اَ۬للَّهِ وَفَضْلࣲ) الشهداء يستبشرون بثواب اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى وفضله زيادته عليه (وَأَنَّ اَ۬للَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ اَ۬لْمُومِنِينَ) بل يأجرهم. الشهداء وصفهم اللّه في القرآن بأنّهم أحياء عند ربّهم. الشهيد لا يسقط إلا وقد اهتدى لمقعده في الجنة، يوضع على رأسه تاج الكرامة، ويغفر له جميع خطاياه ويشفع في سبعين من أهل بيته، ويزوج اثنتين وسبعين من الحور العين، فيستبشرون هذا الثواب وما زادهم اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى من فضله الذي لا حد له. وأنواع الشهادة كثيرة: الشهيد في المعركة شهيد ومن ماتت بجمع، أي امرأة ماتت بالولادة شهيدة، وامرأة ماتت بكرا عذراء، وامرأة ماتت بالغيرة، من صبرت على الغيرة حتى
الله الرعب في قلوب الكفار فتخلفوا عن الميعاد، مدحهم اللّٰه بقوله (اِ۬لذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ اُ۬لنَّاسُ)
نعيم بن مسعود هو فرد ولكن يتكلم عن جماعة (إِنَّ اَ۬لنَّاسَ) أبا سفيان وأصحابه (قَدْ جَمَعُواْ لَكُمْ) الجموع ليستأصلوكم (فَاخْشَوْهُمْ) ولا تأتوهم ( جَزَادَهُمُ ) ذلك القول (إيمنا تصديقا بالله ويقينا (وَقَالُواْ حَسْبُنَا اَ۬للَّهُ) كافينا أمرهم (وَنِعْمَ اَ۬لْوَكِيلُۖ)) المفوض إليه الأمر وهو الله، وخرجوا مع النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم فوافوا سوق بدر فألقى اللّٰه الرعب في قلب أبي سفيان وأصحابه فلم يأتوا وكان معهم تجارات وباعوا وربحوا[2] (فَانقَلَبُواْ)
رجعوا من بدر ( بِنِعْمَةࣲ مِّنَ اَ۬للَّهِ وَفَضْلࣲ) بسلامة ورزق (لَّمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوٓءࣱ) من قتل أو جرح (وَاتَّبَعُواْ رِصْوَالَ اللَّهِ) بطاعته ورسوله في الخروج (وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَظِيمٍۖ) على أهل طاعته (اِنَّمَا ذَٰلِكُمُ) القائل لكم إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم ( اُ۬لشَّيْطَٰنُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَآءَهُۥ )
الكفار (بَلَاَ تَخَافُوهُمْۖ وَخَافُونِ) في ترك أمري {إِل كُنتُم مُّومِنِينَۖ لا تخافوا أولياء الشيطان، خافوني أنا اللّٰه إن كنتم مؤمنين حقا. هذه الكلمة التي قالها الصحابة «حَسْبُنَا اَ۬للَّهُ وَنِعْمَ اَ۬لْوَكِيلُۖ» بها نصر الله تبارك وتعالى كل نبي وكل ولي من أول الدهر إلى آخر
إبراهيم لما ألقي في النار ماذا قال؟ سأله جبريل: ألك حاجة؟ قال: أما إليك فلا. قال:
ألك حاجة إلى الله؟ قال: نعم. قال: سله ينجيك من هذا، قال: علمه بحالي حسبي عن
سوالي، قال: حسبنا اَ۬للَّهِ ونعم الوكيل، "قَلْنَا يَتَارُ كُوبه بَرْداࣰ وَسَلَٰماً عَلَيٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَۖ". وأصحار النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم لما تجمع الكفار وقالوا «إِنَّ اَ۬لنَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُواْ لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمُۥٓ إِيمَٰناࣰۖ وَقَالُواْ حَسْبُنَا اَ۬للَّهُ وَنِعْمَ اَ۬لْوَكِيلُۖ فَانقَلَبُواْ بِنِعْمَةࣲ مِّنَ اَ۬للَّهِ وَفَضْلࣲ لَّمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوٓءࣱ) .
واحد من الصالحين يقول: عجبت من شخص توعده رجل أو خاف من شيء وهو يعلم حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وهو يسمع كلام اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى "حَسْبُنَا اَ۬للَّهُ وَنِعْمَ اَ۬لْوَكِيلُۖ فَانقَلَبُواْ بِنِعْمَةࣲ مِّنَ اَ۬للَّهِ وَفَضْلࣲ لَّمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوٓءࣱ"، وأحد نزل به غم وهو يعلم "لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّے كُنتُ مِنَ اَ۬لظَّٰلِمِينَۖ" وهو يسمع اللّه يقول "قَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَهُ مِسَ ألْعَمٌّ، وأحد تُوعد بالقتل وهو يعرف "وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِيَ إِلَي اَ۬للَّهِۖ إِنَّ اَ۬للَّهَ بَصِيرُۢ بِالْعِبَادِۖ" وهو يسمع اللّٰه يقول: " بَوَفِيهُ اُ۬للَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِ مَا مَكَرُواْۖ وَحَاقَ بِـَٔالِ فِرْعَوْنَ سُوٓءُ اُ۬لْعَذَابِۖ". هذه الكلمة من لازمها عدد حروفها أربعمائة وخمسين كل صباح ومساء لا يضره شيء مما خلق الله. يقول الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم (رجعنا من الجهاد الأصغر إلى الجهاد الأكبر) الجهاد الأصغر الجهاد بالسيف والجهاد الأكبر جهاد النفس والهوى والشيطان. شهيد الجهاد الأصغر شهيد وقتيل الجهاد الأكبر صدّيق والصديقون أعلى مقاما من الشهداء.
ولا بد من الرجوع إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى بالكلية ورفض كل ما سواه وعدم الخوف من أي مخلوق كما أكدت الآية: "وَلاَ تَخَابُوهُمْ وَحَابُونِ"، لن يدخل الحضرة إلا من صلى على جميع الكائنات صلاة الجنازة أربع تكبيرات، فينفرد لله تبارك وتعالى لا يرجو غيره ولا يخافه.
قال أبو يزيد البسطامي: اشتغلت بالمجاهدة لإصلاح نفسي اثنتي عشرة سنة، فرأيت زنارا
